newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOXING-VENEZUELA'S BONILLA KEEPS WBA FLYWEIGHT TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-VENEZUELA'S BONILLA KEEPS WBA FLYWEIGHT TITLE.

text.p: Jose Bonilla of Venezuela easily retained his World Boxing Association (WBA) flyweight title when he stopped Japan's Hiroki Ioka in the seventh round on Tuesday.
American referee Rafael Ramos stopped the fight at two minutes 49 seconds of the seventh round in Osaka with the challenger helpless against the ropes.
Bonilla floored Ioka in the second round to take control of the fight.
"The fight went the way we had practised, so I thought I would win from the very first round. Ioka is a good fighter, but today he didn't have a chance," Bonilla said.
"I was never able to set the pace and I feel like I have a lot left over," Ioka said.
Bonilla, who took the title from Thailand's San Ploenchit last November, improved his record to 22 wins, including 11 knockouts, against three losses.
Ioka, former World Boxing Council (WBC) strawweight champion and WBA junior-flyweight champion, was making his third attempt to become Japan's first boxer to win titles in three different categories.
The Osaka fighter, however, suffered his sixth loss against 30 wins with 16 knockouts.
